collabs.title: Extra set of hands Sat for a boiler swap in Clifton. 8 hrs, day rate, you learn
collabs.body:
Swapping an old cast iron boiler in a two-family in Clifton Saturday. Rigging the old one out of the basement is the worst part, so I need a strong back first and a brain second. 7am start, figure 8 hours, maybe 9. Day rate, paid at the end of the day, and I'll show you how the near-boiler piping goes together while we do it.

You don't need to know boilers, kid. You need to show up on time with boots and gloves and not be on your phone. That's the job.

pitches.note: 4 years in, run my own service calls in Hudson. Never done a boiler. Strong, on time, quiet lol.

collabs.title: Extra hand Saturday: rewire on a raised house in Long Branch, day rate
collabs.body:
Honestly this one is a classic shore job. House got raised after Sandy, the electrical got "temporarily" reconnected by somebody years ago, and now we're doing it right. Saturday, all day. I need a helper to pull wire, drill, and keep the job clean while I do the panel side.

Day rate. You'll be up and down ladders and in a crawlspace that's more of a crawl than a space. If you've only done new construction, that's fine, this is a good look at what remodel work actually is.

pitches.note: I'm in the electrical program at the Mercer vo-tech, so I'm a student, not a helper yet, but I've been looking for weekend work for exactly this reason. We've done rough-in in the shop booths and I'm good on a ladder. Hamilton to Long Branch is about 45 minutes and I'd leave early.

collabs.title: Helper needed: heat pump install, Edison, 2 days
collabs.body:
Ducted heat pump replacing an old oil furnace, Edison split-level. Two days, Tuesday and Wednesday.
- Day 1: removal, pad, line set, air handler
- Day 2: wiring with the electrician, startup, cleanup
- Day rate, start 7:30
- You will carry a lot and you will clean up more than you think
- I explain the rebate paperwork at lunch for anyone who wants it

Callbacks cost me more than labor does, so I care more about careful than fast.

pitches.note: ok so some context, my boss in clifton said i can take tuesday and wednesday if i want, he'd rather i see a heat pump go in on somebody else's job before we start doing them. i've never done one start to finish, mostly furnaces and carrying. can i meet you at the house, and do i need anything besides hand tools?

collabs.title: Saturday of water heater swaps around Kearny, need an extra hand
collabs.body:
Three water heaters booked for one Saturday, Kearny and Harrison. My father used to say you can tell a plumber by how he leaves a basement, so the job is half install, half cleanup. Draining, carrying the old tanks up, hauling, and I'll let you do a connection or two if you've done them before.

Day rate. I was a helper like this once and I remember who treated me right. I try to be that guy.

pitches.note: Union City, 4 years of service, I do water heaters most weeks. Worked a Saturday for oldsteam_zig this weekend so I know the drill lol. Can meet you at the first house.

collabs.title: Saturday mini-split install in Wayne, one helper
collabs.body:
Doing a two-zone ductless install on a Cape in Wayne on Saturday, the 29th. One helper. First, you'll help me plan the line set route, because that's where every bad install starts. Second, you'll do the core drilling with me, and third you'll watch the vacuum and the startup, not just hand me tools.

Day rate. Ask me how I know a helper who's never seen a micron gauge learns more in one Saturday than a week of slides.

pitches.note: clifton, so wayne is like 15 min. helper at a small residential shop, mostly furnaces and carrying, i saw one mini split go in but i was in the truck for most of it lol. do you want me there before you start, and should i bring a notebook?

collabs.title: Ride-along for an apprentice interested in commercial: Secaucus fit-out, 2 days
collabs.body:
We are in the middle of a large commercial fit-out in Secaucus and I can bring one apprentice along for two days (Tuesday and Wednesday) to see how a commercial job runs: the morning huddle, lockout/tagout on a live building, how a crew splits up the work.

You will watch, carry, and ask questions on breaks. You will not work on anything energized. Hard hat, safety glasses, gloves and boots are required; the GC also needs your name a few days ahead for a site badge, so I can only take someone who answers quickly. Stay safe.

pitches.note: I started as a helper at a residential shop a few weeks ago and I'd like to see the commercial side before I go much further. I have boots, glasses and gloves, and I'll buy a hard hat. I can take both days off. I'll stop at the Wawa on the way and be early.

collabs.title: Extra hand Saturday: restroom rough-in at a warehouse, Mount Laurel
collabs.body:
Private job this time, no certified payroll: a warehouse adding a restroom group in Mount Laurel. Saturday the 12th, 6:30 start. We will be laying out and roughing in the waste and vent, so you will be cutting, carrying, and holding a level for a while.

Day rate. Here's what I look for when I hire: shows up on time, listens, doesn't need to be told twice. If you have a few years in and want to see commercial rough-in, say so in your pitch.

pitches.note: cherry hill, 2 years in at a residential shop... never seen a commercial rough-in and I'd like to. 6:30 is fine, I'm about 15 minutes away. edit: I'll bring my own level

collabs.title: Helper for a service upgrade on a raised house in Sea Bright
collabs.body:
Another shore one. Raised house in Sea Bright, the meter and service got moved up after Sandy and now the owner wants a real panel and a generator inlet. Monday, all day, maybe a few hours Tuesday. Honestly it's a good one to see if you've never watched a service upgrade from start to finish.

Day rate. Ladders, a lot of them. Bring a harness if you have one, I have a spare if you don't.

pitches.note: electrician helper out of manahawkin, about a year in. mostly remodels, i've never seen a service upgrade start to finish. my boss said i can take monday. i have a harness. edit: i can stay tuesday too if you need

collabs.title: Ride-along Sunday: load calc and duct survey on a Clifton Cape
collabs.body:
Sunday the 20th I'm doing a heat-loss calc and a duct survey on a Cape in Clifton, for a homeowner who wants to know if a heat pump will keep up in January. Bring a notebook. First, we measure every room. Second, we look at the ductwork in the attic, which will be ugly. Third, I'll show you how the numbers turn into equipment size.

Unpaid, it's a learning day, but it's the part of HVAC nobody teaches you on the job. Ask me how I know.

pitches.note: clifton again, so this one's around the corner lol. i've been on a bunch of changeouts now and nobody's ever explained how they picked the size, it's always 'same as the old one'. does it take all day, and should i bring the notebook from the mini split day?

collabs.title: Steam job in Garfield Saturday: need someone who isn't afraid of a basement
collabs.body:
One-pipe steam system in a Garfield two-family that hasn't heated right since the owner's father died. We're replacing vents, skimming the boiler, and fixing pitch on a couple of runs in a basement with 6 feet of headroom on a good day. Saturday, 7am.

Day rate. If you've never seen steam, this is how you learn it, kid: in a dirty basement with somebody who's done it for 28 years. That's the job.

pitches.note: 4 years of service in Hudson, did a couple of steam vents on my own. Saturday's good. I'm not great with customers but fine in a basement lol.
bayonne, about a year as a helper, mostly old buildings, so a low basement doesn't scare me. never touched steam, brother, and i want to. can be there before 7.

collabs.title: Ride-along week at a small shop in Kearny, for a vo-tech grad
collabs.body:
I hire out of the county vo-techs and I've learned the hard way that a kid doesn't know if he wants a small shop until he's done a week in one. So: ride along with my trucks Monday the 28th through Friday. Service calls, a water heater, a repipe if it holds. You'll see the phone ring and the schedule fall apart by 10am, which is the real lesson.

Paid for the days you work, or count it as a tryout. My father hired me this way. I want to do it right.

pitches.note: not a vo-tech grad, brother, so tell me if that rules me out. a year at a shop in bayonne, mostly demo and carrying, and i want to see how a shop that actually teaches runs. i can do the whole week.
